title: Invited: Neuromorphic Architectures Based on Augmented Silicon Photonics Platforms
problem: Designing energy-efficient neuromorphic accelerators that integrate phase-change and III-V materials into CMOS-compatible photonic platforms. System-level modeling of heterogeneous photonic-digital architectures requires simulation frameworks.
motivation: Photonic neuromorphic computing offers potential for dramatically improved energy efficiency and speed compared to traditional electronic architectures.
method: The authors propose augmented integrated photonic architectures leveraging phase-change materials and III-V semiconductors for optical computing operations. They develop a CMOS-compatible fabrication platform that integrates these photonic materials. A gem5-based simulation framework models the photonic accelerator interfaced with a RISC-V processor, enabling system-level performance analysis of speed, energy consumption, and footprint.
key_novelty: Integration of phase-change and III-V photonic materials within CMOS-compatible platforms coupled with gem5-based system-level simulation for end-to-end neuromorphic accelerator modeling.
contributions: Vision for neuromorphic accelerators based on integrated silicon photonics within Horizon Europe NEUROPULS project
CMOS-compatible platform integrating phase-change and III-V materials for photonic neuromorphic architectures
gem5-based simulation platform for accurate system-level accelerator modeling with RISC-V integration
Framework for benchmarking accelerator performance on speed, energy consumption, and physical footprint
limitations: Not discussed; paper presents a vision and framework rather than empirical comparative results.
primary_theme: Photonic neuromorphic accelerator platforms with system-level simulation
